summary.text: Ligdus of Crete vowed to expose any child that was not a boy; when his wife Telethusa bore a daughter she raised the infant Iphis as a son — until the girl fell in love with Ianthe and prayed to Isis on the eve of the wedding, and the goddess changed Iphis into a man.

chapters.title: The hidden girl
chapters.text: Near Phaestus and Gnossus lived Ligdus, poor but honest, and his wife Telethusa. When she was with child he swore to kill the infant if it were a girl, for they could not afford a dowry. Isis appeared to Telethusa in a dream and forbade the exposure; when a daughter was born the mother lied and named her Iphis after the grandfather.

chapters.title: The betrothal
chapters.text: Iphis grew up with a girl's face but a boy's dress, and no one suspected the fraud except the nurse. When the time came to marry, Ligdus betrothed Iphis to Ianthe, fairest of the Cretan girls — and Iphis loved her with a love that seemed impossible, for both seemed maidens to the world.

chapters.title: Isis answers
chapters.text: On the eve of the wedding Telethusa and Iphis prayed in Isis' temple. The goddess nodded; the horns of the crescent moon shone, and sistrums rattled. When mother and daughter left, Iphis walked with a lengthened stride, darker face, and short hair — a man in form. Venus and Hymenaeus came to the marriage fire, and Iphis took Ianthe as his bride.
